title: A seasonal covariance test retains persistent W2 changes in eight of 110 field-kinematics dust candidates
abstract: We test whether fixed offsets between NEOWISE observing seasons can explain long infrared changes in published dust candidates. We use a verified campaign visit table and a covariance score with separate seasonal means, two annual pair alignments and deletion of each single pair. The main cadence cuts retain 5810 sources. Eight of 110 low-offset candidates with field kinematics pass a local W2 control test, versus 39 of 3659 controls. All eight were variable in the source study. Thus persistent changes remain after removal of fixed seasonal offsets. However, among non-young candidates with published W1-W2 excess above 0.3 mag, 4 of 20 pass, versus 44 of 267 hot-colour blends. A W2-stratified test gives probability 0.703. This small-sample null result shows that persistence alone does not locate the emitting source. It does not establish equal population rates. Injections show strong dependence on signal shape. The method cannot remove slow calibration drift or variable blends, the strict cadence cut excludes some strong candidates, and field kinematics are not stellar ages. This is a new audit and method on existing observations, not new photometry. Code, input hashes, aggregate results, new W2 statistics, figures and offline reproduction instructions are included.
